thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a long-context smoke harness against the KV cache and I'm seeing steady memory drift. TL;DR: RSS climbs ~3-5MB/min after ~30k tokens and doesn't fully reclaim on eviction. Putting raw notes + commands below. Need someone to triage.
sam: link to artifacts? :eyes:
maria: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/long-kvcache-1823456789 (run id 1823456789) — key files: /artifacts/telemetry.json, /artifacts/jemalloc.txt, /artifacts/heap-graph.svg
leon: skimmed the telemetry quickly — looks like fragmentation increases as we hit many small KV inserts. Reuse rate drops when fragment sizes > 64k. Could be fragmentation + allocator retention.
jia: what exact command did you run? can we reproduce locally?

maria: here is the harness command I used:

```
./bench_kvcache \
  --workload=longflow \
  --tokens=100000 \
  --batch=auto \
  --seed=42 \
  --dump-telemetry=/tmp/run-1823456789.json \
  --kvcache-eviction-policy=LRU \
  --kvcache-max-bytes=8g
```

maria: excerpt from jemalloc (trimmed):
```
allocated: 4.1G active: 4.8G metadata: 48M resident: 5.2G retained: 2.9G
active minus allocated = 0.7G -> fragmentation
```

maria: and tactical log lines from runtime:
```
[KVCache] token_idx=32768 evicting=4 fragments_reused=1 free_bytes=245760
[KVCache] token_idx=65536 evicting=6 fragments_reused=0 free_bytes=198912
[KVCache] token_idx=98304 evicting=8 fragments_reused=1 free_bytes=163840
```
sam: hmm fragments_reused is very low. That suggests our reuse heuristic doesn't match this workload (many slightly different prefixes). Could be collision with batching/kernels that alter prefix structure.
patrick: quick hypothesis: compaction threshold too high; if fragments are small and numerous the allocator keeps many arenas. Two quick experiments: 1) toggle kvcache compaction to be more aggressive (e.g., --kvcache-compact-threshold=0.3) and 2) force jemalloc purge between phases (`mallctl` purge) to see if retained decreases.
leon: also check our continuous batching logic — if we coalesce requests differently across iterations we might be creating many short-lived KV inserts that fragment the pool. Add a deterministic batch size run: `--batch=1` vs `--batch=128` and compare.
maria: I can run both experiments. I'll start with the compaction flag and a controlled batch size run. Will push results back here.

perf-bot: scheduled run 1823456795 for bench_kvcache (params: longflow, tokens=100k, kvcache-compact-threshold=0.3) — started at 1823456795

maria: quick note — I also tried an artificial reuse workload (repeat prefixes) and the reuse rate improved and retained memory stayed flat, so the issue reproduces only on variegated long flows. That points at fragmentation + allocator behavior rather than core leak.
jia: good repro notes. Please include the telemetry snapshot and jemalloc stats as attachments to the ticket.

maria: will do. Opening an INF ticket now with run id + artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345 — assigned to runtime perf.

sam: ping me on the ticket if you need help isolating the allocator side. I can spin a tiny C repro that simulates our fragment sizes and exercise jemalloc arenas.

patrick: also worth adding a regression test to our long-context suite that asserts retained/resident/allocated divergence stays below X after steady-state. We can gate on that in CI to catch regressions early.
maria: agree — adding checklist to INF-2345: reproduce, toggles (compaction, batch), jemalloc-purge, minimal C repro, CI regression test. I'll upload initial diff for the CI check later today. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: run 1823456795 completed — logs and telemetry uploaded to https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/long-kvcache-1823456795

leon: great, thanks. once we have both runs (compact vs default) we can compare heap graphs. If compaction helps, consider lowering default threshold and add targeted compaction during heavy long-context requests.
maria: thanks all — I'll post results here when the runs finish and attach the heap graphs.
